script:
1 · Full VO Script
This is a read-through script for the narrator/voice artist — every line that gets spoken, in order, with timecodes. Per the brief's own style guide ("voiceover minimal — prefer on-screen text + interview SOT"), most of the runtime carries no narration at all; those beats are marked as text-only or SOT-only so the artist knows to stay silent. Deliver in a neutral South African accent, unhurried, declarative rather than salesy — closer to a documentary narrator than an ad voice-over.

Section 1 — The Challenge (0:00–0:45)
0:00 title card
No VO — logo hold over black, ambient music only.
Two shootable openings — confirm which before scripting further
Option A (as brief, needs verification): keep the closed-beach framing only if NMBM confirms a partial/seasonal closure still applies at time of shoot.
Option B (recommended, currently defensible): open on the Markman Canal odour complaints instead — same emotional beat (community bearing the cost of an overloaded system), verifiably current as of June 2026. VO below is written for Option B; swap "Brighton Beach" back in if Option A is confirmed live.
0:05–0:15 drone
No narration — ambient wind/water only, per style guide. Let the pictures do the opening.
0:15"Fishwater Flats treats more than sixty percent of Gqeberha's wastewater. When the plant runs at the edge of its capacity, this is where it shows first — in the canals, the estuary, and the communities living alongside them."
0:23 interview
NMBM Official SOT — no VO under it. Suggested line to elicit on camera: something close to "the infrastructure here has been under severe strain" (see Section 3 question sheet).
0:31 stock sequence
Text-only, no VO: "8.5 million tons of organic waste landfilled in SA annually" / "R59 billion annual load-shedding cost" / "Eastern Cape: chronic water scarcity".
0:39"One site. One integrated solution." (spoken softly under the map animation, doubling the on-screen text — optional: can run as text-only instead if the edit feels VO-heavy by this point.)
Section 2 — The Solution (0:45–1:30)
0:45"The Fishwater Flats Biogas Facility is being built on the existing municipal site — turning a liability into a multi-revenue green infrastructure asset."
0:53"Municipal sludge and food waste go in. Three mesophilic co-digesters break it down. What comes out is biomethane, electricity, food-grade carbon dioxide, clean water, and fertiliser — five revenue streams from one process."
1:13 live pilot
No VO — let the genset run under its own sound, on-screen stat only: "Phase 1 Pilot Plant — operational now, 50 kWe exported to NMBM LV grid".
1:20 interview
Darius Boshoff SOT carries this beat alone (co-digestion explainer, see question sheet).
Section 3 — Benefits (1:30–2:30)
entire section
By design, no VO here — music drives, on-screen icon cards carry the ten benefit statements verbatim from the storyboard. Do not add narration; it will fight the rapid-cut rhythm.
2:23 interview
Straits Energy Principal SOT closes the section (see question sheet) — no VO under or after.
Section 4 — Proof of Concept & Vision (2:30–3:45)
2:39"The land is there. The feedstock is there. The partnerships are in place."
2:47"This is what Phase 2 and 3 will look like once construction is complete — three high-solids digesters, a biomethane upgrading train, and a cryogenic CO₂ unit, all on the footprint you just saw from the air."
3:12 interview
Yaniv Scherson SOT — EPC credibility beat, no VO under it.
3:24–3:34 ground
No VO — CNG loading and CO₂ vessel shots run on ambient sound and on-screen stats only, exactly as scripted in the storyboard. This is deliberate: the brief calls these the highest-engagement shots in the Victor Valley reference, and narration over them would undercut that.
3:34"Fishwater Flats Biogas Facility. Powering a sustainable future for Nelson Mandela Bay."
Section 5 — Call to Action (3:45–4:00)
entire section
No VO — end card text carries agreements, timeline and contact details. Music fades to silence on the final frame.
60-Second Social Cut — VO Differences
The vertical cut is music-first with almost no narration. If a VO pass is wanted for the social edit specifically, the only two lines that earn their place are:

0:05"One site. One integrated solution."
0:56"Financial close, July twenty twenty-six."
2 · Interview Video Layout & Cutting Grammar
The diagram above (in chat) shows the repeating pattern; this section spells out the specs behind it.

Frame & composition
Element	Spec
Framing	Medium close-up, rule-of-thirds, subject's eyeline just off-lens toward an off-camera interviewer — never straight down the barrel.
Indoor setup	Warm window light or soft key, background bokeh with a plant/project image or drawings visible but out of focus. Indoor = strategic / financial narrative
Outdoor setup	Natural daylight, subject standing at relevant equipment (CHP unit, WWTW perimeter, Brighton Beach/Markman canal). Outdoor = technical / operational narrative
Audio	Lav + boom backup on every setup. Outdoor setups need a dead-cat windscreen — coastal wind will otherwise wreck the take.
Continuity	Same subject, same wardrobe, both setups shot same day where possible — avoids a visible "different day" tell when the edit intercuts indoor/outdoor.
Cutting rhythm inside a soundbite
No SOT clip runs longer than 8–12 seconds before a cutaway — this is the single biggest thing separating a polished corporate doc from a talking-head video. The cutaway is 2–3 seconds of B-roll matched to whatever the subject is describing at that moment (say "co-digestion" → cut to the feed buffer tank; say "CO₂" → cut to the cryogenic vessel). Return to the same interview setup after the cutaway, not a jump-cut within the same shot.

Lower thirds
Timing	Spec
In	Fades in 2 seconds after the cut to that speaker — never on the cut itself.
Hold	4 seconds, then fades. Reappears if the same speaker returns after 30+ seconds away.
Content	Name (Barlow Condensed Bold, white) / Title & organisation (Barlow, sub-green) — matches the block-flow diagram's type system, not a generic broadcast template.
VO vs SOT vs silence — the rule
VO and interview SOT never overlap. One or the other, never both at once.
Music ducks to −24dB under any spoken line (VO or SOT) and returns to full level in the gaps.
Ambient location sound (ocean, CHP hum, truck idling) stays up under VO at a low bed — it should never go fully silent under narration, or the cut will feel sterile.
Section 3's rapid-fire benefits run on music and on-screen text alone — this is the one stretch of the video with no spoken word of any kind. Resist the urge to fill it.
Interview scheduling logic
Shoot both setups (indoor + outdoor) for each subject back-to-back on the same site visit. Suggested order, grouping by location to minimise crew travel:

Order	Subject	Location	Setups
1	Darius Boshoff	FWF site	Indoor (site office) + outdoor (Phase 1 pilot CHP)
2	NMBM Official	FWF site / council office	Indoor (council chamber) + outdoor (WWTW perimeter)
3	Straits Energy Principal	Office + Brighton Beach or Markman Canal	Indoor (boardroom) + outdoor (per the fact-check above)
4	Yaniv Scherson	Anaergia office	Indoor only — mirrors his existing VVWRA appearance, no outdoor setup needed
3 · Interview Question Sheets
Expanded from the brief's talking points into an actual interview run-sheet: warm-up questions (for comfort, not for the edit), on-camera questions mapped to the story beat they serve, and a safety-net follow-up if the first answer runs short or off-message.

NMBM Official
Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality · Water & Sanitation — municipal anchor
Warm-up (off the record, builds ease)
How long have you worked in water and sanitation for the metro?
What does a normal day at Fishwater Flats actually involve?
On camera — maps to Section 1 (0:23)
Describe the infrastructure strain at Fishwater Flats in your own words — what does "out of compliance" actually look like day to day?
What was the community impact, in the areas you're closest to — the estuary, the fishing community, the canal complaints?
Why did NMBM enter the Sludge Supply Agreement and Lease with Straits Energy rather than fund the upgrade itself?
What does "zero cost to the municipality" actually mean in practice for a metro that's under this much budget pressure?
What does this project mean for jobs and local economic activity in Gqeberha?
Safety-net follow-up
If answers run short: "If you had to explain this partnership to a resident who just wants clean water and reliable power — what would you tell them?"

Darius Boshoff
Transactional Engineering Advisor · Straits Energy — technical authority
Warm-up
What first got you into anaerobic digestion / waste-to-energy engineering?
On camera — maps to Section 2 (1:20) and Section 4 (2:30 pilot)
In plain terms, what is co-digestion, and why does mixing food waste with sludge produce more biogas than sludge alone?
Walk me through the three CSTR digesters — scale, output, why three rather than one large unit.
Why does biomethane to Perseverance matter for the automotive sector specifically?
Food-grade CO₂ is described as "the opportunity nobody talks about" — why is that market underserved right now?
The Phase 1 pilot is running today — what does it prove that a feasibility study on paper can't?
Safety-net follow-up
"If an investor only remembers one sentence about the technology, what should it be?"

Yaniv Scherson
Chief Operating Officer · Anaergia (EPC Partner) — global credibility
Warm-up
How many of these co-digestion systems has Anaergia deployed globally?
On camera — maps to Section 4 (3:12)
You appeared in the Victor Valley video for a similar system — how does Fishwater Flats compare in scale and feedstock profile?
What makes Gqeberha's feedstock mix (municipal sludge plus regional food waste) particularly well suited to this design?
Anaergia went from preliminary design through to EPC on this project — what does that continuity give the client that a hand-off between firms wouldn't?
What's the honest technical risk on a project like this, and how is it engineered out?
Safety-net follow-up
"Why should a South African municipality trust a technology platform proven mostly overseas?"

Straits Energy Principal
Straits Energy Holdings · Project Developer — investor / deal narrative
Warm-up
What was the moment you knew this project was financeable?
On camera — maps to Section 3 (2:23) and Section 5 (close)
Take me from feasibility study to R600M financial close — what was the hardest milestone to clear?
Why does DBSA Green Fund backing matter to other investors evaluating this deal?
Nelson Mandela Bay has one Fishwater Flats — but South Africa has 850-plus municipal WWTWs. Is this genuinely replicable, or is this site unusually favourable?
Financial close is targeted for July 2026, COD July 2028 — what happens in the gap for a partner who wants in now?
Closing line for camera: who exactly are you looking to partner with, and on what — CO₂ offtake, biomethane offtake, EPC/O&M, or equity?
Safety-net follow-up
"If this deal closes on schedule, what's the one number you want people to remember?"

Running order in the edit (for the editor, not the interviewer)
NMBM (crisis, human stakes) → Darius (technical proof) → Straits Principal (benefits close) → Yaniv (credibility, closes Section 4) → Straits Principal again (CTA close). Each subject is used twice at most; nobody appears back-to-back.
notes:
PROJECT PROMOTIONAL VIDEO BRIEF AND REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION
Document Reference: FWF-BIO-PROMO-VID-REQ-2026-04-11
Prepared by: Straits Energy Holdings www.straits.energy
Date: 11 April 2026
Purpose: To provide a precise, bankable creative brief for the videographer and graphic
design team to produce a high-impact promotional video as supporting project
documentation for financial close, investor presentations, stakeholder engagement, and
NMBM/EPC/O&M partner approvals. The video forms part of the finalised project
information memorandum (PIM) deliverables and will be used in DBSA, Energy trader, gas
offtaker, biofertilizer offtaker, and DTI-CIP reporting packages.
1. Video Objectives
Clearly articulate the multi-dimensional value of the Fishwater Flats (FWF) Biogas Facility
as a financed, co-digestion anaerobic digestion plant located on municipal-owned FWF
Wastewater Treatment Works (WWTW) premises.
Position the project as a landmark infrastructure solution delivering biomethane,
electricity, cryogenic food-grade carbon dioxide, and fertiliser while utilising FWF WWTW
sludges and selected food waste residues.
Drive stakeholder confidence by demonstrating environmental compliance, revenue
certainty (PPA, CO₂ offtake, gate fees, carbon credits), and measurable socio-economic
returns.
Target runtime: 3:30–4:00 minutes (editable 60-second cut for social/media).
Style: Corporate documentary – clean, professional, authoritative, with drone/3D CGI, liveaction pilot footage, subtle motion graphics, and understated South African ambient
soundtrack (no voice-over overload; use on-screen text and minimal narrator where
required).
Aspect ratio / deliverables: 16:9 UHD (4K), vertical 9:16 social cut, English subtitles,
colour-graded for corporate branding (Straits Group SA palette).
2. Video Structure and Content Outline
Section 1: The Challenge – Problems Solved in Nelson Mandela Bay (0:00–0:45)
Visuals: Archival/news footage or B-roll of FWF WWTW outfall, ocean pollution, landfill
sites, water restrictions in arid Eastern Cape, load-shedding impacts, and community
protests (use stock or licensed material only; no sensationalism). 
Narration/key messages (supported by on-screen facts):
 - Deteriorated municipal sludge treatment infrastructure at FWF WWTW resulting in
untreated solids discharge to sea, environmental non-compliance, and public outcry.
 - Unsustainable landfilling of organic/food waste residues.
 - Water scarcity and recovery challenges in an arid region.
 - Municipal infrastructure strain, energy insecurity, and lack of localised renewable
baseload power, heat, and green gas.
 - Missed opportunities for job creation, fertiliser supply, and industrial symbiosis (e.g.,
brick-kiln feedstock, CO₂ offtake).
Section 2: Project Solution – Simple Block Flow Diagram (0:45–1:30)
Animated block-flow schematic (2D/3D motion graphics, clean engineering style consistent
with PIM Annexure D 3D model):
 - Inputs: Primary & secondary sludges from FWF WWTW (pre-thickened to ~12–14 % TS)
+ selected food waste residues (FOG, liquid organics, source-separated streams per Waste
Mapping Report).
 - Core Process: Anaerobic co-digestion in high-solids mesophilic CSTR digesters (3 × units,
Phase 2/3 design).
 - Outputs:
 - Biogas → Upgrading → Biomethane (CNG for tube trailers / piped virtual gas to
Perseverance and on-site users) + renewable baseload electricity & heat via 2 MWe CHP
(embedded generation into FWF 22 kV ring main).
 - Cryogenic food-grade CO₂ (liquefaction plant, 30 tpd nominal, offtake in place).
 - Stabilised digestate → Dewatering → Organic fertiliser (farm application) + brick-kiln
feedstock.
 - Water recovery/recycle streams to support arid-region industrial and municipal reuse.
 - Overlay simple process icons and mass-balance call-outs (e.g., ~2.5 MWe Phase 2 scaling
to 5 MWe with co-digestion).
Section 3: Multi-Dimensional Benefits & Impacts (1:30–2:30)
Rapid-fire, visually linked benefit sequence with icons and real metrics (sourced from PIM
and Waste Mapping Report):
 - Sustainable food waste disposal & landfill diversion. 
 - Enhanced water treatment & recovery in water-stressed region.
 - Organic fertiliser production for local agriculture.
 - Municipal infrastructure improvement (sludge stabilisation at no cost to NMBM).
 - Ocean life protection (elimination of solids discharge).
 - Job creation in agri/energy sector (construction, O&M, supply chain).
 - Feedstock supply to local brick kilns.
 - Localised green gas supply (CNG filling points + 7.5 km biomethane pipeline).
 - Renewable food-grade cryogenic carbon dioxide (industrial offtake).
 - Renewable baseload heat & power for the local grid (PPA with NMBM + Etana Energy
peaking).
Section 4: Proof of Concept & Vision (2:30–3:45)
Real-life snippets of the operational Phase 1 pilot plant (50 kWe modular demonstration –
live footage of CHP, digester, feedstock handling, power export to NMBM LV).
Drone fly-over of current FWF WWTW site “as-is” (existing infrastructure, consolidation
tank, available land per Annexure D).
Transition to 3D model / layout fly-through (use supplied PIM 3D renders + any updated
EPC layout):
 - Show full Phase 2/3 plant integration on municipal premises.
 - Highlight interfaces: waste delivery points (external organics), gas pipeline to
Perseverance, CNG loading, CO₂ tanker bay, digestate loading for farms/brick kilns, water
recycle lines.
 - Animated overlays of impacted businesses: farm fertiliser application projects, industrial
water recovery users, brick-kiln feedstock deliveries.
Closing shot: Aerial view of integrated site with glowing renewable energy graphics and text
“Fishwater Flats Biogas Facility – Powering a Sustainable Future for Nelson Mandela Bay”.
Section 5: Call to Action / Closing (3:45–4:00)
On-screen: Project sponsors (Straits Energy Holdings, Energidrop, Sustain Energy Assets,
Norad, DBSA, Get Invest and other partners), key agreements in place (Sludge Supply
Agreement, SLA, Lease agreement, CO₂ Termsheet, PPA, EPC/O&M selection), timelines
(Financial Close Jul 2026, COD Jul 2028), and contact for partnership opportunities. 
3. Technical & Production Requirements
Assets to be supplied by Straits Energy Holdings:
 - Phase 1 pilot plant access for the contractor to shoot live-action footage (already
operational).
 - Full 3D model files (PIM Annexure D) and latest EPC layout drawings (Preliminary Scope
doc dated 2 March 2026). TO BE DISCUSSED – potentially easier to redraw?
 - High-resolution site photography / drone stills of FWF WWTW.
 - Approved project logos, colour palette, and branding guidelines.
 - Fact-checked data tables/metrics from PIM, Waste Mapping Report, CO₂ offtake
Termsheet, Biomethane offtake for the automotive sector, and Sludge Supply Agreement.
Graphic Design Elements:
 - Clean engineering-style block-flow animation (vector-based, scalable).
 - 3D fly-throughs (photo-realistic, consistent with Anaergia/EPC 3D model).
 - Motion-graphic icons for each benefit.
 - Subtle data visualisation (e.g., waste volumes from Waste Mapping Report).
Legal & Compliance:
 - All footage and graphics must comply with NMBM site access protocols, EIA conditions,
and confidentiality notices.
 - Include standard disclaimer: “Project under development – subject to financial close and
regulatory approvals.”
 - Music and stock footage must be royalty-free with full licensing provided.
Delivery Format & Files:
 - Master 4K ProRes 422 HQ + H.264 versions.
 - Raw project files (After Effects/ Premiere Pro) for future edits.
 - Closed-caption SRT file.
 - 60-second teaser and still-frame thumbnails.
4. Project Administration
Review & Approval Process: Two review rounds (draft cut + final). All factual content to be
signed off by Transactional Engineering Advisor prior to final render.
Timeline (target): Concept storyboard within 7 days of briefing; final video within 21 days
of asset handover. 
Budget Guidance: Fixed-price quotation required covering pre-production, production,
post-production, and revisions.
This specification document shall form part of the project’s finalised promotional and
marketing collateral pack and will be appended to the PIM update for financial close. Please
provide a detailed creative treatment and quotation by 18 April 2026.
Should any clarification be required on technical interfaces, mass balances, or 3D assets,
contact Darius Boshoff.
Project site with main gas pipeline heading 7.5 km to Perseverance Industrial area.
Swarkops river mouth to the north east. Brighton Beach currently closed due to ecoli and
sewerage effluent not being treated and running into the sea effecting ocean life and
fishermen livelihood.
